title: Constant commutative-ring sheaf modules and canonical scalar restriction
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site, with objects in universe $u$ and arrows in universe $v$, and $B$ a commutative ring in universe $\max(u,v)$. Write $R=\underline B$ for its constant commutative-ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define $\mathrm{Modules}(J,B)$ to be sheaves of modules over the underlying ring sheaf of $R$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\mathrm{Fixed}(J,B)=\operatorname{Sh}_J(C,\operatorname{Mod}_B)$. The functor $\mathrm{restriction}:\mathrm{Modules}(J,B)\to\mathrm{Fixed}(J,B)$ first restricts scalars along the canonical isomorphism between the underlying ring sheaf of the constant commutative-ring sheaf and the constant ring sheaf, then applies restriction along the constant-ring sheafification unit [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction]. Thus it retains sections and restriction maps and gives each section its $B$-action through that unit. This is the specified functor itself; no claim of exactness, tensor compatibility or equivalence is included.
